text:
maya: Quick PSA — my carry-on zipper tore in a Lyft heading to the airport. Flight in ~6h. No tailor nearby. Any quick emergency fixes? 😬
kevin: Oh no. Paperclip through the zipper pull as a temp handle, then wrap with tape. Or use a small binder clip to keep it closed.
alexa: If the slider popped off you can thread the teeth and squeeze the slider gently with pliers. Hotel concierge usually has a sewing kit + safety pins too.
sam: Walgreens or CVS at/near most airports sells a tiny zipper repair kit. If you're at ORD, Terminal 2/3 has a shop. Otherwise, shove fragile stuff into a plastic bag inside the bag to avoid spills.
luggage-bot: Found a nearby cobbler & sewing shop: https://maps.app.goo.gl/example-link (open now; call first).
kevin: Another trick: loop a luggage tag or shoelace through both zipper pulls and lock them together with a padlock or twist-tie. Prevents gap from opening.
alexa: Compression packing cubes help if you need to move contents into a spare tote quickly. Also, a safety pin through fabric + zipper teeth works as a last-resort hold.
maya: Thanks all — grabbed safety pins from concierge, used a binder clip + duct tape inside. Flight made it. You're my heroes :heart:
sam: Pro tip for next time: stash a tiny repair kit in your laptop sleeve. Worth the 2oz.
kevin: Vote: should we add a mini sewing kit + a roll of 1" duct tape to the team offsite shared bag? :thumbsup: / :thumbsdown:
alexa: :thumbsup: from me. Also consider a micro pliers set.
maya: Agree — let's add it to the shared bag list. Also tagging @travel-planning so it's on the next offsite checklist.
luggage-bot: Saved note to shared-items list.
